title: Early state width fits gave no clear NRCS runoff quantile score gain at 470 sites in 2013-2025
abstract: We tested a simple correction to archived NRCS April 1 forecasts of April-July adjusted runoff. We fitted state width factors on 4,811 cases in 2000-2012 and kept forecast medians fixed. On 5,612 later cases at 470 western US sites in 2013-2025, the correction gave -0.18% loss reduction, with a 95% whole-year interval of -1.29 to +0.89%. An interval that also fitted the factors again in resampled training years was -3.67 to +0.77%. A pooled factor and yearly updated factors also gave no clear gain. The state correction increased mean width by 10.6% and coverage from 78.7% to 82.8%. The early New Mexico factor was 0.600. Later New Mexico coverage fell from 92.9% to 68.2%, while its score gain remained uncertain. Thus this simple width correction did not establish better later forecast scores. Prior campaign work had already described the same later archive, so this is a retrospective time split, not a blind forecast test. Thirteen test years, archive revisions, adjusted flows, selected sites and one factor for all quantiles limit inference. Code, source hashes, aggregate evidence, an independent scalar audit and a static figure are included. Raw sources and record-level tables remain external.

display.caption: Early state width fits gave no clear later score gain. Panels show score intervals, fitted width factors, annual score changes and example state coverage. All intervals keep sites in a year together. State comparisons are exploratory and pointwise. Arizona and South Dakota use the pooled factor.
